title: Building AI For All: Amjad Masad & Michele Catasta
talk_summary: Amjad Masad and Michele Catasta present Replit's AI-for-all rollout and the training of Replit's own small code-completion model (replit-code v1.5 3B), emphasizing inference-optimized small models, data quality, and fast deployment. The talk is mostly product announcement and model-training detail, with only a few transferable engineering mechanisms.

takeaways.technique: Small inference-optimized model for high-volume narrow tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They train a small 3.3B model specifically optimized for inference latency (small vocab, GQA, flash attention) rather than benchmark scores, and serve it for code completion instead of a large general model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of our models are actually optimized for inference rather than for being awesome at benchmarks
takeaways.numbers: 3.3B params, 4K context, >200 tokens/sec single-stream, P95 latency target <250ms

takeaways.technique: Cut model-deploy cold-start from 18 min to 2 min
takeaways.what_they_do: An engineer reworked the deployment pipeline (dependency/build caching tricks) so scaling to load reacts in minutes rather than tens of minutes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: brought this number from 18 minutes to just two minutes

takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate generated code by executing it against test harnesses across many languages (HumanEval/MultiPL-E) rather than judging text similarity.
They give the model prefix (top of file) and suffix (bottom of file) context, and make the format aware of the underlying abstract syntax tree, improving completion quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the top of the file is your prefix the bottom of the file is your suffix

takeaways.what_they_do: They filter aggressively (remove autogenerated/minified/non-parseable code) and repeat a small high-quality subset several epochs, citing that loss after 4-5 repeats matches novel data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your loss curve after you repeat data four or five times is going to be comparable to training on a novel data set
takeaways.numbers: 1T tokens, ~200B across 5 epochs, 30B curated for continued pretraining
